root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `parse_content_length()` formats `*p` in the shared parse-error logger, it must verify `p < end`; EOF error paths must not execute the char-formatting branch.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable EOF witness reaches the shared `error:` label with `p == end` and still executes the `LM_ERR("parse error near char [%d][%c]\n", *p, *p)` branch. The fixed code inserts `if(p<end)` around that branch and sends EOF to a separate over-end message, while the one-byte append witness still reaches the guarded char-log branch with `p < end`.

nodes.state: At the shared `error:` label on the vulnerable EOF witness, the parser cursor `p` has already advanced to `end`, so any char-formatted access through `*p` names the first byte past the bounded Content-Length span.

The protected `LM_ERR("parse error near char [%d][%c]\n", *p, *p)` branch is the source-level sink: it dereferences the same parser cursor captured at `error_log_guard` when formatting the offending character.

edges.relation: The same parser cursor `p` captured at the missing EOF guard is the pointer dereferenced by the char-formatting error logger.
